name: Dream 7B: Diffusion Large Language Models
problem: Autoregressive models generate strictly sequentially, so decoding cannot be parallelised and in-context infilling or arbitrary-order generation is awkward.
mechanism: A 7B diffusion language model that refines sequences in parallel through iterative denoising instead of generating left to right, achieving its results through simple training techniques rather than a new architecture: autoregressive-based LLM INITIALISATION (start from an existing AR checkpoint rather than from scratch, which is the main practical difference from LLaDA), context-adaptive token-level noise scheduling, and a diffusion backbone built on an AR LLM. Generation: begin from a masked or noised sequence, iterate the denoiser, and unmask tokens under a confidence schedule. FLOP consequence as in all masked diffusion LMs: T full-sequence forward passes for an L-token output, so FLOPs are roughly T times one full-length prefill and are much higher than autoregressive decoding; the payoff is parallel generation of many positions per step plus the flexibility of arbitrary-order generation, infilling, and a tunable quality-versus-speed tradeoff via the step count and per-step token budget. Open weights are released.
speedup_reported: Reports consistently outperforming existing diffusion language models on general, mathematical and coding tasks, plus superior planning ability and inference flexibility including arbitrary-order generation, infilling, and tunable quality-speed trade-offs. No tok/s speedup ratio with baseline and settings is published in the abstract, so the claim being recorded is the tunable quality-speed frontier via denoising-step count, not a speedup.
notes:
arXiv preprint; no journal-ref. Engine support verified: llama.cpp carries LLM_ARCH_DREAM, lists it in llm_arch_is_diffusion(), and has a dedicated conversion/dream.py. No native Dream row appears in the vLLM supported-models list consulted. The AR-initialisation trick is the practically important detail because it means diffusion LMs no longer require the from-scratch budget LLaDA needed, which is why adoption among practitioners picked up in 2025. Model weights and code were released by the authors.
